text:
sara: heads up — we've got a customer report: p99 latency for model-texgen-v2 in us-west-2 jumped from ~1.2s to ~9-12s around 17:30 UTC. ticket #INC-4823. they see intermittent 500s too.
vikram: thanks — is this for hosted or dedicated? which instance size?
sara: hosted. route=texgen-v2-prod, node group rdw-west2-gpu-a10x. recent deploy?
jess: deploy-bot shows no prod deploys to that pool in the last 6h. commit hash unchanged.
dave: I pulled infra metrics: GPU mem usage steady at ~92% for healthy times, but since 17:20 we see spikes to 99% and frequent cuda OOMs (kernel retries). Might be fragmentation + KV growth.
sara: can you paste the nvidia-smi and our runtime logs around an OOM?
dave: pasted below:
```
# nvidia-smi sample
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85       Driver Version: 525.85       CUDA Version: 12.0     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A10          On           | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off | N/A                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|   GPU   PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory Usage          |
|   0     8421      C   python3                         32400MiB / 33792MiB     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Runtime log snippet:
```
2026-04-01T17:21:03Z runtime ERROR request_id=abc123 OOM: cudaMalloc failed size=2147483648
2026-04-01T17:21:03Z runtime WARN  request_id=abc123 falling back to CPU execution (slow path)
2026-04-01T17:21:05Z runtime INFO  request_id=abc123 completed latency_ms=9123 path=fallback_cpu
2026-04-01T17:21:07Z runtime ERROR allocator fragmentation ratio=0.78 attempts_to_free=3
2026-04-01T17:21:09Z runtime INFO  KVCache size for model=texgen-v2 entries=1387 total_kv_bytes=6.2GB
```
vikram: KV growth to 6.2GB on top of model footprint is suspicious. Are customers sending very long contexts?
jess: support thread shows one enterprise customer running 200k-token unpacked contexts (not compressed) via streaming. that's likely the KV blowup.
sara: ok that matches. hypothesis: long context requests cause KV cache to grow per-session without eviction; fragmentation + cudaMalloc/free patterns cause OOM and fallback to CPU which explains the p99 tail.
dave: repro plan: spin single A10 node, send a mix of short and a few very long-context requests from same session to trigger KV retention; measure allocator fragmentation and nvidia memory. I'll run a small script.
vikram: share repro script and exact curl so support can reproduce. Also add quick mitigations we can roll ASAP.
dave: repro script below (short):
```
# reproduce_kv_growth.sh
for i in {1..300}; do
  # 295 short requests, then one long
  if [ $i -lt 295 ]; then
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"texgen-v2","input":"hello world","session_id":"sess-oom"}'
  else
    long_ctx=$(python3 - <<'PY'
print("
".join(["lorem ipsum"]*50000))
PY
)
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d "{"model":"texgen-v2","input":"$long_ctx","session_id":"sess-oom"}"
  fi
done
```
jess: thanks. immediate mitigations we can do without code changes: 1) throttle per-session token rate and aggregate context length (router guard); 2) temporarily pin this pool to a smaller max_sequence or reject >N tokens; 3) route large requests to a dedicated high-memory pool or to a CPU-heavy fallback that has bigger mem but slower latency (avoid OOM causing fragmentation).
vikram: agree. additional infra mitigations: enable cudaMallocAsync pool (if not already), increase per-GPU reserved pool (cudaMalloc pool) to reduce fragmentation, and tune our allocator free-thresholds. We can also configure KVCache eviction policy to LRU with max_entries or aging TTL.
dave: quick patch candidate: when we detect OOM we currently do fallback_cpu but we keep fragmented GPU allocator; we should add a recovery path that attempts to drain and reset the CUDA arena for that worker after an OOM to avoid repeated OOMs. patch should be low-risk.
sara: customer impact mitigation timeline: - immediate (next 30m): add router guard to cap incoming context length to 64k tokens for hosted default and return 413-like response with guidance; enable emergency throttle for suspect sessions. - short (2-6h): route large-session traffic to a high-mem pool; increase reserved GPU pool by 1-2GB. - medium (1-3d): deploy allocator tuning + KV eviction TTL and telemetry.
jess: can support team message customers: apologize, say we're investigating GPU memory pressure causing timeouts and we have temporary throttles. ask for sample session_id and approximate context lengths.
dave: I ran repro and captured allocator stats: fragmentation ratio climbs with repeated large-context requests; after OOM we saw many cudaMalloc retries which cause delays of seconds while runtime tries reclaiming/defragmenting. This matches p95->p99 spikes.
vikram: low-risk prod rollback: add router rule to detect session-level avg_seq_len > 32k and auto-promote to dedicated-highmem or reject. I can roll that in ~45m.
sara: owners: vikram for router guard + pool routing, dave for allocator quick-recovery patch, jess for customer comms and support triage. I'll create follow-up RFC for KV eviction policy and long-term telemetry.
ops-bot: incident created INC-4823 assigned to vikram, dave, jess. severity=P2.
jen (support): customer reported they will try to reduce sent context; asked to be notified when we throttle.
vikram: I'll start the router guard rollout in canary 1 then 3, then wide if stable. posting checklist: 1) config change to cap request.max_context_tokens=64k (can be overridden for Dedicated contracts) 2) route policy for large_context -> highmem pool 3) add metric alarms for per-node fragmentation ratio >0.6 4) quick-restart worker after OOM triggers (controlled)
dave: adding notes to runtime: implement `--reclaim-after-oom` which does cudaDeviceSynchronize + cudaIpc cleanup + reset arenas for that worker. will open PR and link here.
sara: thanks team. I'll update ticket and ping customer. keep this thread for comms and paste PR links here when ready. :thumbsup:
